header.name: Introduction to Algebraic Geometry with Applications
header.description: Algebraic Geometry is the study of the geometry of the solution space of a system of polynomials (or set of common zeros of the set of polynomials). The fundamental objective of the subject is to study the algebraic varieties. Algebraic Geometry is a subject which connects diverse fields of Mathematics such as Algebra, Topology, Complex analysis, Number theory, Differential geometry, Cryptography, Coding theory etc. In this course, we study basic Algebraic Geometry consisting of algebraic varieties, maps between varieties etc. We elaborately discuss projective geometry, which is the centre of the subject. We cover some classical results of Algebraic Geometry e.g. Hilbert's basis theorem and Hilbert's Nullstellensatz theorem. As an application, we study algebraic curves, which are the one-dimensional algebraic varieties.
prerequisites_desirable: MTH 212 (Algebra I) or equivalent, or should have familiarity with Ring theory (definition and examples of ring, ring homomorphism, ideals), Field theory (definition and examples of fields) and basic Topology (definition of open and closed sets).

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students should be able to provide examples of varieties (affine and projective) of any dimension and understand map between varieties.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students should understand celebrated Hilbert's basis theorem and Hilbert's Nullstellensatz theorem. They can apply these theorems to solve problems.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students can classify types of singularities on plane curves and resolve singularities by blowing up points. They can understand intersection numbers on plane curves.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students should be able to apply the understanding of genus of a curve to calculate the genus of plane curves. They can also understand the Riemann-Roch theorem on curves and its applications.

lecture_topics: Affine algebraic set and it’s properties
Multiplicities at a point on a plane curve
Blow-up to resolve singularities on curve
